public_rationale: The forecast states no deadline. Under the contract, it is settled early only if a major US tech index falls 20% or more from its peak in a decline widely tied to AI-investment concerns. That decline must also come with documented spillover to the wider economy or a sharp fall in AI investment. Al Jazeera reported that the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6% on October 22, 2026, amid worries about AI spending. After that fall, the index was about 5.8% below its all-time high of October 6, 2026 (e1). That is well short of the 20% threshold. The cited evidence does not show spillover to the wider economy or a sharp fall in AI investment. Market data after October 23, 2026 was not reviewed. Under the contract, an open-ended forecast cannot be contradicted just because no qualifying decline has happened yet. The outcome stays unresolved.
limitations: "Brick wall" and "part of our economy" have no defined threshold or scope.
Only one market snapshot was reviewed (e1, reporting moves through October 22–23, 2026). Market data after October 23, 2026 was not checked.
No AI capital spending series or wider economic indicators were reviewed.
Reports about Chinese AI stocks were left out because the statement concerns the US tech industry.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The tech industry and part of the economy are heading for a crash driven by AI leaders' hype.

statement.excerpt: The tech industry — and part of our economy — is accelerating at speed into a brick wall, driven by people like Sam Altman, Dario Amodei, Marc Benioff, and Larry Ellison, all men that are incentivized to have you value their companies based on something other than what their businesses actually sell.

from_speaker: The tech industry — and part of our economy
is accelerating at speed into a brick wall
driven by people like Sam Altman, Dario Amodei, Marc Benioff, and Larry Ellison
our_interpretation: Plain reading: the tech industry, and the parts of the economy tied to it, will suffer a sharp collapse linked to the AI boom.
No deadline is stated, so this is an open-horizon forecast.
The causal attribution to particular executives is not scored. Only whether the crash happens is scored.
criteria.support_condition: A broad, sharp tech-sector collapse tied to AI, such as a major tech index falling into a bear market (20% or more from its peak) together with steep cuts in AI investment or wider economic damage.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, it cannot be contradicted by the absence of a crash. It could only be undercut if the AI investment cycle clearly matured without a collapse over a long period.
